I've been farming these 4.1 mu for 40 years now. At 63, I'm not as strong as I used to be, and with just me in the household, I have to be careful with labor. Cotton has been my crop for a long time — I know what it needs.

This year, I'll plant my usual improved Bt cotton variety in mid-April. The Bt seed costs more than traditional seed, but it saves me from spraying for bollworm every week like I used to when I was younger. That matters now because I can't carry tanks around like I used to. I'll do rotary tillage to prepare the beds — my neighbor helped me with the machine last year and it worked fine, so I'll do the same.

For fertilizer, the extension agent says I should use 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, but I've found 15 kg is enough if I apply it right. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and topdress with urea when the plants start flowering in July. I can't afford to overdo it — every jin of fertilizer is cash out of my pocket, and at my age I can't take big risks. I'll use about 6 kg of phosphorus and 7 kg of potassium per mu too, mixed in with the basal dressing.

I have my well, so I'll irrigate three times: once before planting to get the soil moist, once in July when the heat hits and the flowers are setting, and once in August for the bolls. Pumping isn't free — the electricity adds up — but a dry July can ruin everything, so I won't skip it. I'll spray pesticide four times this season. The Bt cotton handles the bollworm, but I still get aphids and spider mites in July. I watch the fields every morning, and if I see damage, I spray. No point spraying if there's nothing there — that's just wasting money.

If the weather cooperates and we don't get a bad drought, I expect around 420 kg of seed cotton per mu. Last year I got 430, but I'm getting older and I want to be realistic. That's my plan.
